details:
/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]

Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: The standalone stall loop in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (from about line 24893) already goes through every candidate that carries a pipeline label, using the prefetched `_candidate_details_json` comments. `orchestrate_lib.py` `STALL_RECOVERY_ACTIONS["ai:clarification"]` (`auto_respond_clarify`, `auto_respond_clarify`, `escalate_human`) already ends in `escalate_human`. So the change belongs inside that loop. When there is no clarify output, meaning no `<!-- ai:clarification-questions -->` comment and no clarify answer comment, the first recovery posts a `/reclarify` comment with a dedup marker in place of `auto_respond_clarify`. Today `auto_respond_clarify` would answer questions that were never asked. If the marker is present and there is still no clarify output, the second miss goes to the existing `escalate_human`. Option C would put two code paths on the same issue. Option B adds a new variable and turns off current behaviour. On the issue's 6-hour default: the existing per-phase setting `STALL_THRESHOLD_CLARIFICATION_MINUTES` (built-in default 60 in `DEFAULT_PHASE_STALL_THRESHOLDS`) already controls this phase, and an operator who wants 6 hours can set it to 360. Keeping one threshold avoids a second clock for the same label.
Q2: The code shows this is very likely what happened to #146. In `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` (lines 931-946), a held security follow-up gets the `ai:clarification` label and is skipped with no comment. In the poller (lines 24948-24955), a held verdict logs `STALL_SKIP ... reason=security_dependency_held` and moves on, also with no comment. A hold whose detail is `closed_without_ai_merged` or `unverified` never releases on its own. Re-running clarify (option C) would get around the same-file security ordering gate, which breaks the "security first, fail closed" rule. Option B keeps the silence that caused the incident. Option A keeps the gate and makes the hold visible. It works as follows:
- The poller posts one advisory comment per dependency, with the marker `<!-- ai:security-dependency-held:<issue>:<depends_on> -->`.
- The comment names `.depends_on` from the `security_dependency.py` verdict and the detail (`open`, `closed_without_ai_merged` or `unverified`).
- For the two details that cannot release on their own, the comment says a maintainer must act.
- It is posted only when the cached comment history is complete and has no marker yet. If comments are unavailable, nothing is posted, so no duplicates.
- The comment does not start with `/reclarify` and does not use the clarification-questions marker. This keeps the release-marker check and the Q1 "no clarify output" check unchanged.

SETUP REQUIRED: none. Neither decision depends on a placeholder or on an operator provisioning anything.
